text.p: International Thoroughbred Breeders Inc said Thursday it has removed six members of its board of directors, named four new directors, and elected Frank Leo chairman.

The company also said that the New Jersey Casino Control Commission, a state regulatory agency, also accepted a proposed settlement between its former chairman and chief executive, Robert Brennan, and the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement, which would require Brennan to place his common stock shares into a liquidating trust.
The shares would be placed in the trust contingent upon bankruptcy court approval within 60 days, it said. The company also said the settlement was approved over Brennan's objections.
Brennan resigned from the company on November 2.

The company said it does not believe the commission's action would have an effect on its day-to-day operations. International Thoroughbred Breeders said Brennan also has told the company that he also is in negotiations to divest himself of his shares through a sale to an independent group of investors.

Meanwhile, a U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge granted Brennan a temporary restraining order preventing ITB's board of directors from implementing a shareholder rights plan, which the board had planned to consider, the company said.
Brennan, the company's largest shareholder, is the beneficial owner of 2,904,016 shares, or about 30 percent of the company's stock.

The New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement filed a complaint with the Casino Control Commission seeking to prohibit the company's two race tracks, Garden State Park and Freehold Raceway, from conducting business with any casino licensee.

The complaint was based on a U.S. District Court ruling that found Brennan liable of violating federal securities laws between 1982 and 1985. Brennan has denied the claims and is appealing the decision.
The company's new chairman, Leo, is the beneficial owner of 536,201 shares of ITB common stock.
The six board members removed were: Arthur Winkler, Roger Bodman, Joel Sterns, Clifford Goldman, Robert Peloquin and Steve Norton.
Elected as directors were: Frank Leo, John Mariucci, James Murray and Frank Koenemund.
